rich_text.plain_text: How big should it be?

text.content: How big should it be?

rich_text.plain_text: Bigger than your first instinct. The most common mistake in pale rooms is a small print marooned on a large wall, which reads as an apology. The old rule of thumb holds: art hung above furniture wants to be roughly two-thirds the width of what's beneath it, either as one piece or as a group hung tight enough to read as one. Above a standard sofa that means one 50 x 70 print is a minimum, a pair is better, and a trio earns the wall. On its own wall, a single 50 x 70 in a frame holds a surprising amount of space, because the frame and the margin do half the work.

rich_text.plain_text: Will colour break the look?

text.content: Will colour break the look?

rich_text.plain_text: No, and believing it will is how rooms end up beige. The white walls aren't the point of the style, they're the backdrop for the things that are. A saturated print in a white room isn't a risk, it's the reward: the room was calm so that something could speak. If everything on the wall whispers, the wall is just texture.
